sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 shows the north-western part of Iselin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, between Middlesex Avenue along the right edge and Hillcrest Avenue and the Correja Avenue grid on the left. The cross streets run north-east to south-west: Diaz, Fiume, Trento and Trieste across the upper left, then Pershing, Fiat, Sonora, La Guardia and Oak Tree Road down the sheet, with Correja, Marconi and Hillcrest Avenues crossing them. Kennedy Street and Kennedy Place curve across the upper middle around a fan of narrow lots, and Goodrich and Hunt Streets run along the top edge beside a small triangular block. Harding Avenue and Iselin Boulevard cross at an angle at the lower right, where the Lincoln Highway is lettered at the corner of the sheet. Most blocks are numbered 15 to 49 and 201 to 208 and are built up with detached frame dwellings, a few stores and the Woodbridge Public School No. 15 with its auditorium. A clothing factory stands beside Oak Tree Road and a motion picture theatre at Oak Tree Road and Marconi Avenue, and the fire department building is on Harding Avenue near Middlesex Avenue. A stream and a pond cross the lower left, and a large north arrow and the scale bar sit in the lower left corner. The right-hand strip beyond Middlesex Avenue repeats outlines of sheet 3 with the names Coakley, Wright, Vernam and Sutton Streets lettered but little drawn.
notes: Wilson (Washington) Avenue is Wilson Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
La Guardia Avenue is Laguardia Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Kennedy Street and Kennedy Place are both lettered on the curved road; OpenStreetMap has Kennedy Street.
Iselin Boulevard is not under that name in the OpenStreetMap extract and was not used as control.
Oak Tree Road at Correja and Hillcrest Avenues lies 14 to 17 m from the modern road line and those junctions were rejected; Harding Avenue at Middlesex Avenue was rejected at about 17 m.
Street names on the right edge strip (Coakley, Wright, Vernam, Sutton) belong to sheet 3.
Some small lettering (John, Coakley, Lincoln Highway) was read on crops reduced 2.8 times; medium confidence.

Iselin NW, 100 ft; Diaz, Fiume, Trento, Trieste, Pershing, Fiat, Sonora, La Guardia, Oak Tree Road, Correja, Marconi, Hillcrest, Harding, Iselin Blvd. One part. Oak Tree Road junctions at its western end rejected (14-17 m).

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the Iselin district west of the Middlesex and Essex Turnpike at 100 feet to an inch, from McLean Street and Warwick Street across the top to Oak Tree Road and Green Street along the bottom. Middlesex Avenue forms the left edge, with Auth Avenue, Dow Avenue and Talmadge Avenue running north to south through the sheet, crossed by Goodrich, Hunt, Kennedy, Coakley, Wright, Vernam and Sutton Streets. The blocks, numbered 50 to 75 and 209 to 213, are long and narrow and mostly unbuilt, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds and many lots marked by their numbers only. The Lincoln Highway cuts diagonally across the right half beside the multi-track railroad drawn along the Middlesex and Essex Turnpike, where a contractors yard and machinery storage plant and an auto repair shop front the highway. St. Cecelia's R.C. Church stands on Sutton Street at Oak Tree Road and the Union Protestant Church just south of Oak Tree Road, and Woodbridge Public School No. 6 and a fire department building are on Green Street near Cooper Avenue. At the right edge the sheet shows the streets east of the turnpike (Madison, Cherry, Main, Canal and Grand) with Benjamin Avenue and the label Iselin. A large compass rose is placed in the upper left centre, and the scale bar crosses the lower right.
notes: Auth Avenue and Talmadge Avenue are lettered with (St.) after Av.; the meaning of the parenthesis was not determined. OpenStreetMap has Auth Avenue and Talmadge Avenue.
Green (Oak Tree Rd.) at the foot of the sheet is Green Street in OpenStreetMap; the Lincoln Highway meets it at Auth Avenue.

The Middlesex & Essex Turnpike is Middlesex Turnpike in OpenStreetMap; its junctions with Canal and Cherry Streets are 11 to 22 m from the drawn ones and the turnpike streets and Benjamin Avenue (13 to 18 m off) were left out of the control.
McLean is lettered McLEAN, not Mc Lean as in OpenStreetMap; Warwick was read from the letters WARW cut at the edge of a crop (medium confidence).
A curved road near Dow Avenue carries a partial label ending in PARK, not read in full; a word reading BLOCK near the Iselin label was also not read in full.

Iselin, 100 ft; Middlesex Av, Auth, Dow, Talmadge, McLean, Warwick, Goodrich to Sutton, Lincoln Hwy, Middlesex & Essex Turnpike, Green (Oak Tree Rd). One part. Middlesex Turnpike group east of the railroad and Benjamin Avenue left out (11-22 m); east strip past Talmadge uncontrolled.

sheet-4-1.description: Sheet 4 part 1 is the Avenel and Colonia area west of Chain O'Hills Road, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 60 degrees from north (the street grid runs diagonally across the page). The main road is Chain O'Hills Road, which runs down the right half from Midfield Road past North Hill Road and Valley Road to New Dover Road, the road also lettered Colonia Boulevard on its western side. Left of it lies a grid of unopened subdivision streets, Union, Fairview Avenue, Hudson Avenue, Outlook Avenue and Middlesex Avenue, with Maplewood Avenue and Sussex Street at the bottom; many are marked not open and the blocks, numbered 80 to 94 and 305 to 311, are nearly empty. A cluster of houses stands around Chain O'Hills Road and North Hill Road, and a few farm and dwelling buildings at the right edge near West Hill Road and a tile-roofed brick house near New Dover Road. Public School No. 2 stands at the foot of Maplewood Avenue. At the lower left a Pennsylvania Railroad line with several tracks passes beside Colonia Station and a gate house. Long Hill Road, Mac Farland Road and North Hill Road cut off the upper centre as a subdivision of long lots, and the oval title stamp with the word Avenel is at the upper right. The inset at the upper left, the Colonia Country Club on Colonia Boulevard, has its own compass and is a separate part.
notes: New Dover Road in the east is lettered Colonia Boulevard where it runs west of Chain O'Hills Road; OpenStreetMap has New Dover Road.

The Outlook Avenue junctions with New Dover Road and Sussex Street and the Fairview Avenue junction with New Dover Road were 5 to 7 m off the modern lines and were left out; Maplewood Avenue at Sussex Street too.
The street label Mac Farland was read from a crop cut at the edge (RLAND RD.) and the overview (MAC FARLAND RD.); medium confidence.
The inset at the upper left (Colonia Country Club, Located 3 Miles N.W. of Town Hall) is not part of this mask.
Hudson Avenue, Union and several other streets in the lower left grid are marked Not Open and are not in OpenStreetMap under these names.
Avenel/Colonia, 100 ft, turned about -63 degrees. Part 1 main (6 points). Part 2: inset at upper left, Colonia Country Club on Colonia Boulevard, own compass; not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Colonia Country Club on Colonia Boulevard ("Located 3 Miles N.W. of Town Hall") (no street junction; needs step 6b: one hand-picked point with px_per_ft 3.94 and north_deg (arrow about -70 degrees)).

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the central Avenel district at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 7 degrees from north. St. George's Avenue crosses the sheet from the upper right to the lower left, meeting Chain O'Hills Road at the centre-left, and Avenel Street runs down the sheet from that point as the main axis. East of it lie Thorpe Avenue, Ella Avenue (marked not opened in places), Hyatt, Woodruff Avenue, Prospect Avenue, Remsen Avenue and Demorest Avenue, laid out as long parallel blocks numbered 101 to 126 between the cross streets Butler, Lord and Wylie. A subdivision of Midfield Road, East Hill Road and Long Hill Road occupies the upper left, with North Hill Road and Valley Road at the left edge. The district is lightly built, mostly frame dwellings with a few stores near Avenel Street and Prospect Avenue, a lumber yard at the centre and the D. Grossman cement block works in the upper middle. Other buildings are an auto repair shop on St. George's Avenue and a few small pink-coloured masonry buildings. Six and eight inch water pipes follow Avenel Street and Remsen Avenue. A large north arrow stands in the upper left, the oval title stamp with the word Avenel is at the upper right, and the scale bar is at the lower left.
notes: St. George's Avenue is Saint Georges Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the sheet's Avenel street is Avenel Street.
Woodruff Avenue at Wylie was rejected at 11 m and not used.
Several blocks of Ella Avenue and Thorpe Avenue are marked Not Opened.
The street label Lord was read on the overview and on a reduced crop (medium confidence).
Avenel centre, 100 ft; St. George's Av, Chain O'Hills Rd, Avenel St, Thorpe, Ella, Woodruff, Prospect, Remsen, Demorest. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the eastern side of Avenel at 100 feet to an inch, turned about 8 degrees from north. Butler runs diagonally across the left half and meets Remsen Avenue and Douglas Avenue at the centre. Ella Avenue, Woodruff Avenue, Prospect Avenue, Remsen Avenue and Demorest Avenue run north-east to south-west across the left side, and Hyatt, Avenel and Minna Avenue are drawn at the lower left. East of Butler the large blocks numbered 128 to 134 are cut into very long narrow lots that run between Prospect Avenue, Remsen Avenue and Douglas Avenue, with a scattering of dwellings, a co-operative building and a few outbuildings along Douglas Avenue. Cosy Corner runs across the top edge. State Highway Route No. 25 is a broad diagonal strip across the lower right of the sheet, with blocks 512 and 513 on either side of it, and Woodbridge Avenue forms the right edge. Much of the lower half is blank, the area west of the highway belonging to the next sheet. A small group of dwellings at Avenel and Hyatt, a few water pipes of 6 and 8 inches and several fire hydrants are marked. The north arrow is at the left, the oval title stamp with the word Avenel at the top right, and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Butler is Butler Street in OpenStreetMap; the junction of Butler Street with Prospect Avenue was rejected at 12 m.
Cosy Corner and its junctions with Prospect Avenue and Ella Avenue were not detected.
State Highway Route No. 25 is today US 1; the highway itself was not used as control.
Minna Avenue is lettered in small italic capitals at the lower left and was read on a reduced crop (medium confidence).
Avenel east, 100 ft; Butler, Remsen, Douglas, Cosy Corner, State Highway Route 25 (US 1), Woodbridge Av. One part, 7 points.

sheet-7-1.description: Sheet 7 shows the western edge of Avenel at 100 feet to an inch, most of it open land. The Pennsylvania Railroad main line, drawn as four tracks marked R.R., runs down the sheet a little left of centre, with Inman Avenue parallel to it on the west, crossing large undivided blocks numbered 135, 136 and 137. At the lower left, Avenel Street runs diagonally across the bottom of the sheet past Park Avenue, 5th Avenue, Kingston Avenue and West Side Avenue, with frame dwellings and a few stores; Cedar runs parallel to it to the north, where Woodbridge Public School No. 4 with its auditorium, two separate class rooms and a small public library stand. The Avenel depot is drawn beside the tracks on Avenel Street. East of the railroad, the large brick works of the Steel Equipment Corporation, makers of office and bank equipment, fill block 141 at the bottom, with its own siding, assembling rooms, shipping and storage. At the right edge a laid-out subdivision runs along Cornell, with the cross streets Vassar Place, Dartmouth Avenue, Lehigh Avenue, Yale Avenue and Harvard Avenue platted into narrow lots but not yet built on (blocks 142 to 146). A heavy line boxes off the upper right corner for an inset of the Boynton Lumber Company at Sewaren (part 2), which is not part of this map. The north arrow points straight up the page; adjoining sheets 8, 10 and 11 are marked along the edges.
notes: Inman Avenue is South Inman Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Park Avenue is West Park Avenue.
Kingston Avenue (south of Avenel Street) has no street of that name today; it may be today's Livingston Avenue (not used as control).
Cedar may be today's Cedar Street (not used as control).
Placed from Cornell Street junctions and three junctions on Avenel Street.
Works: Steel Equipment Corp'n, Woodbridge Public School No. 4, Avenel Depot.

Avenel west edge, 100 ft. Part 1: Inman Avenue, the Pennsylvania Railroad, Avenel Street (Park, 5th, Kingston, West Side Avenues), Cornell subdivision (Vassar to Harvard), Steel Equipment Corp. Part 2: boxed inset at upper right, Boynton Lumber Co. at Sewaren on West Avenue (State) with Old (Beach) Road, own north arrow about -25 degrees.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Boynton Lumber Co., Sewaren, West Avenue (State) and Old (Beach) Road (no surviving junction inside the inset (Old Road south of Mechanic Street is gone); its site is on West Avenue / State Street south of Sewaren; needs step 6b: carried points from sheet-23 if it draws the same blocks, or parcel corners).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the western part of Avenel, a residential village on the Pennsylvania Railroad line in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Rahway Avenue is the diagonal spine, running from the top of the sheet at about the centre down to the lower edge a little right of centre. To its west are small blocks of narrow lots between Trinity Place, Maple, Walnut and Homestead Avenue, a set of streets fanning out from a slanting northern boundary, and below Dartmouth Avenue a regular grid of long blocks between Cornell, Oak, Lehigh Avenue, Yale Avenue and Harvard Avenue. Much of this southwestern grid is laid out in lots but unbuilt, and the large block 166 holds a single institutional building. East of Rahway Avenue the blocks run between Edgerton Avenue at the top, Homestead Avenue, Blanchard Avenue, Cedar (Edgar) Avenue and Harvard Avenue at the bottom, cut by Chestnut, Holly, Mereline, Harriott and Blanford Avenues. These east blocks are the most built up, with frame dwellings drawn in yellow and a few brick buildings in pink, a Greek Catholic school on Mereline Avenue and a cement block manufactory at Cedar Avenue. The upper left of the sheet is blank, carrying only the compass rose and the block number 137, since that ground is drawn on another sheet or not subdivided. Block numbers 147 to 176 appear, with the adjoining sheets 7 and 16 named at the margins and the sheet title cartouche at upper right. A scale bar is printed along Harvard Avenue at the foot.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Edgerton Avenue is Edgerton Boulevard, Maple is North Maple Street, Walnut is North Walnut Street, Holly is Borman Avenue, Blanchard Avenue is Cobb Way, Harriott Avenue is Thayer Avenue, Blanford Avenue is Blandford Avenue, Cedar (Edgar) Avenue is Homer Court, Oak is Oak Street, Cornell is Cornell Street.
Elm at the right edge was not matched to a modern street and was not used for control.
The upper left quarter is blank except for the compass rose and block 137.
Avenel, 100 ft; Rahway Av diagonal, Dartmouth to Harvard Av, Edgerton, Homestead. One part.

sheet-9-1.description: Sheet 9 part 1 is the southern part of Avenel at 100 feet to an inch, with St. George's Avenue along the left side and Prospect Avenue, Remsen Avenue, Demorest Avenue and Minna Avenue crossing the right half on the diagonal. At the left the cross streets Valley Road, Colonia Place, Dover Road, Enfield Road, Middlehill Road and Highfield Road run down to the heavy line near South Hill Road, with the unbuilt blocks 177 to 181 and 190 between them. Thorpe Avenue and the blocks 120 and 182 sit between St. George's Avenue and Prospect Avenue, and Wylie and Smith cross the diagonal avenues in the middle. At the lower right Tappen runs across the foot of the sheet, and Ziegler Avenue and State Highway Route No. 25 are drawn as broad diagonal strips along the right edge. The district is thinly built with detached frame dwellings, an auto repair shop on St. George's Avenue, a hall and a long storage building near Wylie and Remsen Avenue, and a few stores and sheds along St. George's Avenue. A heavy black line near the lower left corner, running from South Hill Road along a bend and down the sheet, separates a different area, with the Middlesex Concrete Products Company plant, that is a separate part. The north arrow stands at the top centre, the oval title stamp with the word Avenel at the top right and the scale bar at the foot.
notes: Middlehill Road is Middle Hill Road in OpenStreetMap; St. George's Avenue is Saint Georges Avenue; Smith is Smith Street.
The sheet is not internally consistent with modern streets: Prospect Avenue, Thorpe Avenue, Remsen Avenue and Wylie junctions were 3 to 8 m from the fit and several were left out.
The area below and left of the heavy line (blocks 515 and 516, Middlesex Concrete Products Co. Plant No. 1, a second north arrow) is a separate part and is not covered.
Woodruff Avenue and Lord Street are lettered at the top edge in small type, read on reduced crops (medium confidence).

Avenel south, 100 ft. Part 1 main (St. George's Av to Ziegler Av / Route 25; residuals 3-5 m on Prospect and Remsen). Part 2 below the heavy line at lower left (Middlesex Concrete Products Co. plant, blocks 515-516, own north arrow); not placed.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: area below the heavy line at lower left: Middlesex Concrete Products Co. Plant No. 1, blocks 515-516 (no usable junction; needs step 6b from sheet-10 or sheet-9-1 (St. George's Avenue)).

sheet-10-1.description: Sheet 10, part 1 is the main map of the sheet: a district of Avenel west of the Pennsylvania Railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with the streets running slightly out of square to the page. A heavy double line runs down the right side and separates this part from the railroad strip beyond. Avenel street crosses the upper third from left to right, with Hyatt above it and Lord below, and Wylie and Smith lower down; the cross streets are Demorest, Minna, Ziegler, Jansen and, near the heavy line, Woodbridge Avenue. A diagonal Hyatt street, with a second label near the top, cuts across the upper blocks, and State Highway Route No. 25 is lettered along the street the sheet names Ziegler Avenue. The blocks, numbered 193 to 205, are laid out in long narrow lots. Dwellings in yellow and a few brick buildings in pink and blue stand along Avenel and Lord and near the top left, while the lower blocks between Wylie and Smith, and the long strip of block 203 beside Jansen Avenue, are laid out but mostly empty. A synagogue and a printing building are drawn near Minna Avenue. Eight-inch and six-inch water pipes are marked along Avenel, Lord and Hyatt. A compass rose with a north arrow is at the lower left, a scale bar and the library stamp at the bottom, and the neighbouring sheet numbers 6, 5 and 9 stand in the left margin and 9 below.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Hyatt is Hyatt Street, Avenel is Avenel Street, Lord is Lord Street, Wylie is Wylie Street, Smith is Smith Street and West Smith Street, Ziegler Avenue is US 1 (State Highway Route No. 25), Woodbridge Avenue is probably East Woodbridge Avenue.
The heavy double line on the right is the division from part 2, which is drawn at another place on the ground (the Avenel station area).
Hyatt Street / Jansen Avenue, Hyatt Street / Minna Avenue and Demorest Avenue / Smith Street were not detected.

Avenel, 100 ft. Part 1 main map west of the heavy line (Demorest to Jansen, Hyatt to Smith). Part 2 strip right of the line: station area on the Pennsylvania Railroad with West Side Av and Pennsylvania Av, placed by a helmert on five hand picks along East Pennsylvania Avenue (low confidence).

sheet-10-2.description: Sheet 10, part 2 is the narrow strip on the right of the sheet, separated from the main map by a heavy double line and drawn at a different place: the Avenel station area on the Pennsylvania Railroad, at 100 feet to an inch. The tracks of the P. R. R. run down the strip, with Avenel street crossing them on a diagonal from upper left to right. West Side Avenue runs along the heavy line on the left and Pennsylvania Avenue forms the right-hand street, with the short cross streets Smith, Meinzer, George, Burnett and Oliver leaving it towards sheet 11. Beside the tracks near Avenel street are a plastic products works (Dur-Econ Plastic Products Co.), with a plaster manufactory, storage and a tile building, a row of stores, and a shirt factory with its light and power note on the east side of the tracks; a club house stands on the east block. Block 204 covers the long lot-divided blocks between the railroad and Pennsylvania Avenue. Inman Avenue, Maple Avenue and Center Street are lettered at the left edge by the heavy line, and the title Avenel with the number 7 for the continuing sheet stands at the top above the tracks. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are drawn along Avenel street and Pennsylvania Avenue, and the footing of the heavy line is marked no exposure along the bottom.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Avenel is Avenel Street, Pennsylvania Avenue is East Pennsylvania Avenue, Smith Street is North Smith Street, Burnett Street is Burnet Street, Inman Avenue is South Inman Avenue.

This strip is a separate part: the main map to its left is about 540 m away on the ground. It is placed only by five hand-picked junctions along Pennsylvania Avenue, so its position across the street and its rotation are low confidence.
Maple Avenue and Center Street are lettered in the narrow space beside the heavy line and were not identified with modern streets.

Avenel, 100 ft. Part 1 main map west of the heavy line (Demorest to Jansen, Hyatt to Smith). Part 2 strip right of the line: station area on the Pennsylvania Railroad with West Side Av and Pennsylvania Av, placed by a helmert on five hand picks along East Pennsylvania Avenue (low confidence).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 shows the eastern part of Avenel between Pennsylvania Avenue on the west and Rahway Avenue on the east, at 100 feet to an inch. Harvard Avenue crosses the top edge, and below it Avenel, Smith, Meinzer, George, Burnett and Oliver streets run across the sheet in a regular grid of long blocks numbered 205 to 315, divided by Cornell and Oak above Avenel and by Manhattan Avenue and Commercial Avenue below it. Rahway Avenue forms the slanting right edge. West of Manhattan Avenue the same cross streets continue at an angle toward Pennsylvania Avenue, and the lots there (blocks 208, 301, 304, 307 and 310) are drawn on a different bearing and carry most of the sheet's houses, drawn in yellow with a few in blue and pink. The central grid is mostly laid out in lots, with dwellings strung along Burnett Street and the north side of Avenel Street, and the large blocks east of Commercial Avenue largely empty. Below Oliver Street a broad band is marked Public Service Trolley Right of Way, with the P. R. R. tracks of the Pennsylvania Railroad beneath it and the Port Reading line crossing Rahway Avenue at the right. South of the tracks is a district of unopened streets: Sylvia and Crescent are marked not open, Court is marked impassable and Ridgedale Avenue not opened, with Bucknell Avenue along the foot, around blocks 316 and 519 to 522. A compass rose is at the lower left and a scale bar at the foot. The adjoining sheets named in the margins are 7, 8, 10, 12 and 16.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Avenel is Avenel Street, Smith is North Smith Street, Burnett is Burnet Street, Pennsylvania Avenue is East Pennsylvania Avenue, Coddington Avenue is East Coddington Avenue, Cornell is Cornell Street, Oak is Oak Street, Court is Court Street, Bucknell is Bucknell Avenue.
Crescent and Sylvia are marked not open, Court impassable, and Ridgedale Avenue not opened.
Bucknell Avenue / Court Street was rejected by the fit (7.9 m) and the lower unopened area has little control.
Avenel east, 100 ft; Avenel to Oliver grid, Pennsylvania Av to Rahway Av; unopened Crescent/Sylvia/Court/Ridgedale district at the bottom uncontrolled. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the Woodbridge district between the Pennsylvania Railroad on the west and Rahway Avenue on the east, from Bucknell Avenue at the top to Carrol Avenue at the foot, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Ridgedale Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet and Rahway Avenue forms the slanting right edge. Bucknell, Lockwood, Hillside, Prospect, Vanderbilt, Craske, Schoder, Wedgewood and Carrol cross it, with East Avenue, Sunnyside Place, Hillside Place, Norman Place and Rose Place on the east side. The area east of Ridgedale Avenue is the more built-up part, with scattered frame houses and some brick buildings along Hillside and East Avenue, rows of narrow lots in blocks 319 to 331, and poultry buildings near Carrol Avenue. West of Ridgedale Avenue the blocks are larger and mostly open, among them the large unsubdivided blocks 601 to 603, and two streets are marked Proposed Street. Hart Products Corporation, a chemical works, stands near the compass rose in block 318. On the left, west of the tracks, are Tyson Bros Inc., vulcanized oil, and R. Gusmer, manufacturing chemicals, with their light, power and watchman notes, in block 317 with the margin marked no exposure. At the lower left Barron, Oak and Railroad avenues bound the lot-divided blocks 324 to 327. A scale bar and the library stamp are at the foot, and the sheet number 11 is printed above the top edge and 15 below.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Prospect is East Prospect Avenue, East Avenue is North East Avenue, Sunnyside Place is Sunnyside Avenue, Vanderbilt is Vanderbilt Place, Craske is Craske Street, Carrol is Carrol Avenue.
Two streets are marked Proposed Street, west of Ridgedale Avenue near Prospect and Vanderbilt.
The fit is second order with 20 points, almost all east of the railroad; the west edge (Tyson Bros, Gusmer, Barron, Oak and Railroad avenues) has no control.
Woodbridge, 100 ft; Bucknell to Carrol Av along Ridgedale Av; west edge (Tyson Bros, Gusmer) uncontrolled. One part, second-order fit.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the western part of Woodbridge village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and continues sheet 14 to the east across Amboy Avenue. Amboy Avenue, also lettered St. George's Avenue, forms the right edge; Wilry and Alwat run across the top, Church, Mawbey and Campbell cross the middle, and Grove Avenue and Green run along the lower part. The streets run in two directions: the cross streets and Lincoln and Washington avenues form a regular grid in the upper right, while Lyman, Leon, Elias, Gorham and Joseph avenues fan out to the lower left at an angle. Thomas Street cuts a long diagonal across the sheet from the upper centre to Green, meeting Decker Place, which is also lettered Thomas, near the lower right. The upper blocks, numbered 605 to 610, are largely vacant lots, and a wide tract, block 333, lies empty at the top right. The most densely built area is the lower right, around Decker Place and Rowland Place, where rows of small frame houses are drawn on the blocks 352 and 353. The southwest is drawn as long, narrow lots with few buildings, along Elias, Gorham, Liberty and Mobile avenues. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the upper left, in the large empty block 332, and the title and the word Woodbridge are at the upper right. The scale bar and the Princeton library stamp are at the foot, and the neighbouring sheets 14 and 18 are named in the margins.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Wilry is Willry Street, Lincoln Avenue is South Lincoln Avenue, Washington Avenue is East Washington Avenue, Church is Church Street, Mawbey is Mawbey Street, Campbell is Campbell Street, Green is Green Street, Thomas is Thomas Street, Alwat is Alwat Street.
Amboy (St. George's) Avenue is Amboy Avenue and Saint Georges Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Amboy Avenue / Church Street and Amboy Avenue / Saint Georges Avenue are excluded as in sheet 14.
East Washington Avenue is partly displaced from its 1929 line: its junctions with Campbell, Grove and Thomas were rejected at 5.5 to 6.3 m. Gorham Avenue / Grove Avenue was rejected at 11 m.
The right margin repeats street labels of sheet 14 (Church St., High St., Dunham Pl., Valentine Pl.).
Woodbridge west of Amboy Av, 100 ft; Church, Mawbey, Campbell, Grove, Green; Lyman to Joseph fan. One part. East Washington Avenue partly displaced (3 junctions rejected).

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the northern part of Woodbridge village between Amboy Avenue on the west and Barron Avenue on the east, from Brown and Freeman Streets in the north to Green Street along the bottom edge, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Amboy Avenue runs down the left edge; in its upper part the sheet labels the parallel road to its east St. George's Avenue, and below Church Street the main road is lettered Amboy Avenue with St. George's in parentheses. Freeman Street crosses the top of the sheet on a diagonal and then turns east along the line of Church Street to Barron Avenue. The cross streets are North, Church, High, Grove Avenue and Green, with Noe Avenue, Linden Avenue, Tisdale Place, Maple, Myrtle and Cedar running north to south between them, and the short Dunham Place and Valentine Place west of Linden Avenue. The upper half is thinly built, with large blocks of frame dwellings, poultry houses and a stretch of Church Street marked not opened west of Noe Avenue. The lower half is denser, with rows of small brick and frame dwellings along Dunham Place, Valentine Place, Maple and Myrtle. Woodbridge High School, with its auditorium and gymnasium, fills the block between Grove Avenue and Green Street at the lower right, and the First Congregational Church and its parsonage stand at Grove Avenue and Barron Avenue. A Masonic Lodge building is drawn on Tisdale Place. Water pipes of 6 and 16 inches are marked on Freeman, Church, High and Green, and a scale bar is printed across Decker and Rowland Places at the lower left. Block numbers 357 to 370 and 556B to 556D and 611 appear, with adjoining sheets 13, 15 and 19.
notes: St. George's Avenue is Saint Georges Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the road lettered Amboy (St. George's) Avenue below Church Street is today's Amboy Avenue.
Dunham Place is also lettered Campbell, and Valentine Place Thomas, in parentheses.
Church Street west of Noe Avenue is marked not opened.
North Street / Saint Georges Avenue was rejected by the fit (8 m): North Street may have moved since 1929.
Woodbridge High School and the First Congregational Church are on this sheet.
Pilot. Woodbridge village north of Green Street: Amboy Avenue (St. George's), Freeman, Church, High, Grove Avenue, Barron Avenue, Linden Avenue. 100 ft; fitted 4.00 px/ft, rotation +2.5. One part.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the centre of Woodbridge village, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, between the Pennsylvania Railroad on the left and Brookfield and Bamford avenues at the lower right. Rahway Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from upper right to lower left. In the upper half Ridgedale and Ridgewood avenues run north from Freeman, with Ellis Place between them, past the large blocks 371, 375 to 377 and the built-up block 372; Martin Terrace forms an east to west street across the middle. Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road enters from the right on a diagonal towards the Barron Public Library, which is drawn in blue beside Rahway Avenue. The lower left is a dense district of narrow lots, with rows of dwellings on Olive Place, Alice Place and Grove Avenue, a contractor's yard, a garage and the First Baptist Church near Nielson. Lower still are Claire Apartments, a large brick building drawn in pink, and a row of houses along Melbourne Avenue and Green. To the right a fan of streets, Alden, Garden, Almon, Bamford and Brookfield avenues, crosses Crampton Avenue at an angle, laid out in long narrow lots (blocks 379 to 394) with houses along the streets. The Pennsylvania Railroad tracks, with the Barron Avenue sheet 14 edge repeating along the left, run down the left side, with the Night Shirt Factory and a machine works beside them. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the right, the title cartouche and the word Woodbridge at the upper right, and the scale bar at the foot. Adjoining sheets 12, 14, 16, 19 and 20 are named in the margins.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Freeman is Freeman Street, Martin Terrace is Martin Terrace, Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue, Alden Avenue is Alden Street, Green is Green Street or East Green Street, Grove Avenue is East Grove Avenue, Trinity Lane was not matched.

The streets around Rahway Avenue, Ridgedale Avenue, Ridgewood Avenue and East Grove Avenue are displaced or rebuilt against their 1929 lines (4 to 11 m); they were left out of the control, so only eight junctions in the east and centre place this sheet and the fit is low confidence.
The west strip beside the railroad repeats sheet 14.

Woodbridge centre, 100 ft; Freeman, Martin Ter, Rahway Av, Crampton fan. One part, 8 points in the east half; Rahway, East Grove, Ridgedale, Ridgewood and Port Reading Avenues left out (4-11 m). Low confidence in the west half.

sheet-16-1.description: Sheet 16, part 1 is the Woodbridge half of the sheet, east of Rahway Avenue and west of the railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. A heavy line along the railroad on the right separates it from a strip of Avenel that is drawn beside it at a different place on the ground. Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road crosses the part on a diagonal from lower left to the junction with Trinity Lane near the railroad. In the upper left a group of streets, Wedgewood Avenue, Leone and Lewis, runs in a fan of long narrow lots (blocks 387 to 389) with houses along them and a tile and poultry building near the top. West of this, block 388 holds the Trinity Episcopal Church and a large open area, and the lower left is block 373, marked Cemetery, with the First Presbyterian Church at its corner. At the centre, near the railroad, the United Railroad Signal Corp., makers of railroad track torpedoes, occupies a group of brick buildings beside Trinity Lane and Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road. The lower part is a gridded district between Garden, Almon, Bamford and Watson avenues and Von Vetchen Avenue, in blocks 390 to 395 and 619 to 620, mostly laid out in lots with scattered dwellings. A compass rose and north arrow are in the upper centre and the word Woodbridge is lettered at the top left. Alden Street appears at the lower left edge, and the sheet numbers 12 and 15 are printed in the left margin.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Wedgewood is Wedgewood Avenue, Leone is Leone Street, Lewis is Lewis Street, Trinity Lane is Trinity Lane, Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue, Alden Street is Alden Street.
Port Reading Avenue (Woodbridge and Roosevelt Road) is realigned against its 1929 line: its junctions were 4 to 14 m off and were left out of the control, as was Alden Street.
Labels on the far left margin (street names beside Rahway Avenue) were not read.

100 ft. Two parts divided by the heavy railroad line: part 1 left, Woodbridge (Wedgewood, Trinity Lane, Von Vetchen, Garden to Watson Avs); part 2 right, Avenel (Rahway, Nielson, Mereline, Harriott, Blanford, Coddington), low confidence.

sheet-16-2.description: Sheet 16, part 2 is the strip of Avenel on the right of the sheet, east of the heavy line that carries the railroad and drawn at a place on the ground distant from the Woodbridge district beside it, at 100 feet to an inch. Rahway Avenue runs down the left side of the strip, with the stubs of Avenel, Smith, Meinzer, George, Burnett and Oliver streets reaching it from the railroad side, and Harvard Avenue at the top beside a water pipe. To the east, Mereline, Harriott and Blanford avenues run north and south between the cross streets Nielson Avenue and Coddington Avenue. The blocks at the top (173 to 176) repeat the blocks at the foot of sheet 8, and below Nielson Avenue the blocks 396 to 398 are long lots laid out but almost unbuilt, with a few frame houses and a brick building along Mereline Avenue. A narrow band of lots with scattered dwellings is drawn along the south side of Coddington Avenue. In the lower half, block 399 holds a public service power house and several outbuildings, a trolley right of way is lettered Public Service Trolley Right of Way, and the Obropta dairy farm stands near the bottom, with a Pennsylvania Railroad line crossing near the foot. A north arrow stands beside Coddington Avenue and the number 11 and the title Avenel are lettered along the top.
notes: Modern names in OpenStreetMap: Nielson Avenue is probably Ashton Court, Harriott Avenue is Thayer Avenue, Blanford Avenue is Blandford Avenue, Coddington Avenue is East Coddington Avenue, Smith Street is North Smith Street, Burnett Street is Burnet Street.

This strip is a separate part: the Woodbridge part beside it is about 1.3 km from it on the ground. Only six junctions place it, three of them on Rahway Avenue with residuals near 5 m, so the placement is low confidence.
Nielson Avenue is matched with Ashton Court on spacing from Harvard Avenue and Coddington Avenue and is not certain.

100 ft. Two parts divided by the heavy railroad line: part 1 left, Woodbridge (Wedgewood, Trinity Lane, Von Vetchen, Garden to Watson Avs); part 2 right, Avenel (Rahway, Nielson, Mereline, Harriott, Blanford, Coddington), low confidence.

sheet-17-1.description: Sheet 17 covers the western end of Woodbridge village along Main Street, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 28 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. Main Street crosses the sheet from left to right, widening to 80 feet east of Oak Avenue, with frame dwellings, small stores and outbuildings along its south side between Mattison Street and St. James Avenue. South of Main the blocks are cut by Grove, Washington and Bergen Street, with Mattison Street, Oak Avenue and St. James Avenue (Dally) running down the sheet; the blocks along Oak Avenue are closely built with dwellings, the rest is thinly built. To the west, King George's Post Road runs diagonally from Main Street to the bottom edge through open land, and the Anness Hollow Tile & Clay Co. works, with its kilns, drying ovens, mixing and machine rooms, stands on the south side of Main at the left edge, served by a curving siding of the P. & R. R.R.. Heards Brook runs from the upper right across the middle of the sheet to the lower left. At the top, Metuchen Avenue runs diagonally with a few dwellings, and Peyser and Dorothy streets lead off it to the north. The upper left corner is boxed off by a heavy line for an inset of the Woodbridge Ceramic Corp. on Green Street (part 2), which is not part of this map. Water pipes of 6 and 12 inches are marked on Main and Oak, and block numbers 401 to 409 appear with adjoining sheet 18.
notes: St. James Avenue is St James Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Grove is Grove Street; Mattison is Mattison Street.
Metuchen Avenue, Peyser and Dorothy junctions were 5 to 8 m from the fit and were left out; Metuchen Avenue may have been realigned.
Both Mattison Street junctions carry 3.5 to 4 m residuals; the street may have moved slightly.
Washington may be today's Anders Way (same position between Oak and St James Avenues); not used as control.
Works: Anness Hollow Tile & Clay Co., makers of hollow tile.

Woodbridge west, 100 ft, north about +28 degrees. Part 1: Main Street from King George's Post Road to St. James Avenue (Dally), Grove, Mattison, Oak Avenue, Washington, Bergen Street, Metuchen Avenue, Heards Brook, Anness Hollow Tile & Clay Co. Part 2: boxed inset at upper left, Woodbridge Ceramic Corp. on Green Street beside the P. & R. R.R., north about -27 degrees.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Woodbridge Ceramic Corp., Green Street at the Reading railroad (no street junction in the inset; the area is rebuilt by the US 1 / US 9 interchange; needs hand-picked control (Green Street line plus one fixed point); none found).

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 shows the part of Woodbridge village west of Amboy Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Amboy Avenue, lettered Amboy (Perth Amboy) Avenue, runs down the right edge, and Main Street crosses the lower half from the left edge to Amboy Avenue. Grove Street runs parallel to it below, with Greenville Street near the bottom edge. The upper half is thinly settled: Green Street and Edgar Street cross the top and middle of the north-south roads Elmwood Avenue and Middlesex Avenue, and Catalpa, Downing, Brighton and James Streets are laid out as lettered lanes of small, mostly unbuilt lots between Elmwood Avenue and Amboy Avenue. Heards Brook winds across the sheet from the right edge to the left, and a large area of farmland and unbuilt blocks, numbered 401, lies on its south side. The lower half is built up with frame dwellings along Main and Grove Streets and the cross streets Columbus, Manor, Dekalb, Desota and Park Avenues and St. James Avenue (Dally). Metuchen Avenue enters at the lower left on a diagonal. St. James R.C. Church and its parochial school stand at Grove Street and Amboy Avenue at the lower right, and a sawmill and a club building are drawn near Amboy Avenue above Main Street. A compass rose and a scale bar for 100 feet to an inch are printed at the upper and lower left, and part of a differently angled subdivision (Gorham and Graham Avenues, Aldine) appears at the top left corner. Block numbers 356 to 358, 401, 402 and 410 to 420 are shown, with adjoining sheets 13, 17 and 19.
notes: St. James Avenue (Dally) is Saint James Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Park Avenue is today's Grady Drive; Greenville is Grenville Street.
Amboy Avenue is not used as control: its junctions here lie 4 to 13 m from the drawn street, probably because the road was widened.
Elmwood Avenue north of Main Street is displaced by 6 to 8 m against the modern line; its junctions with Main and Brighton were rejected and Edgar and Downing carry 2.5 to 3.5 m.
Francis Avenue at the top is the same road as Elmwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Woodbridge west of Amboy Av, 100 ft; Main, Grove, Elmwood, Heards Brook. One part. Amboy and Metuchen Avenues not used (displaced).

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows the centre of Woodbridge village at 100 feet to an inch. Amboy Avenue, lettered Amboy (Perth Amboy) Avenue, runs down the left edge and Main Street, the commercial street, crosses the lower half from Amboy Avenue to the railroad at the right edge. School Street runs north from Main Street through the middle of the sheet, Pearl Street lies near the right edge parallel to the railroad, and Green Street crosses the top. Heards Brook enters at the left and leaves at the right below Park Avenue. The densest building is along Main Street between William Street and Fulton Street, where brick stores, a bank, an electric company building and churches are drawn in pink and yellow; New Street and 2nd Street run parallel to Main Street below it, lined with dwellings. Woodbridge Public School and Woodbridge Grammar School No. 1 stand on Ross Street and School Street, with a Hungarian Reformed Church and a synagogue nearby, and a fire department building is drawn at School and Brook Streets. At the upper right the railroad carries a passenger depot, a freight house and yard tracks. The area north of Park Avenue is largely open lots with scattered frame dwellings. A compass rose is at the lower right, a scale bar for 100 feet to an inch at the bottom, and the sheet notes the date February 1929 and adjoining sheets 14, 15, 18, 20 and 21. Block numbers 421 to 433 are shown.
notes: Amboy Avenue is not used as control (displaced against the modern line).
William Street is displaced against the modern North William Street by 10 to 12 m and was left out of the fit.
Park (Av.) is East Park Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pearl is Pearl Street.
The sheet reaches the railroad at the right edge, the North Jersey Coast Line (Garden State Secondary).
Woodbridge centre, 100 ft; Main, School, Pearl, Green. One part. Amboy Avenue and North William Street not used.

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the area east of the Woodbridge railroad station and the northern part of the Berry brickworks district, at 100 feet to an inch. The railroad runs down the left edge. Beside it, Rahway Avenue leaves Green Street and runs south past Poillon Street to Main Street, where the Woodbridge Lumber Company, the Poillon Pottery Company and several works are drawn. Heards Brook crosses the upper right from Green Street towards the east. East of Rahway Avenue the street grid turns: Moore Avenue, Henley, Harriott and Clinch run north to south and Woodbridge Avenue and Rector cross them, with Berry running diagonally from Main Street south-east. The Town Hall is drawn near Main Street and a municipal garage on Berry Street. At the upper right are Melbourne Court, Garden, Almon, Claire, Bamford, Watson and Brookfield Avenues, laid out as narrow lots, most of them still unbuilt. Gordon, Wallace, Jean Court and Lillian Terrace are rows of small frame dwellings at the lower left, with Eleanor along the railroad. James E. Berry's fire brick works stands at the bottom right beside Woodbridge Creek, with Factory Lane (Berrys Lane) running along the bottom of the sheet. A compass rose is at the right, a scale bar for 100 feet to an inch at the bottom, and the sheet notes February 1929 with adjoining sheets 15, 19 and 21. Block numbers 384, 631 to 640 and 819 to 830 are shown.
notes: Henley is Henley Street, Harriott is Harriot Street, Poillon is Poillon Street in OpenStreetMap.
Wallace, Jean Court and Lillian Terrace, and Eleanor, do not agree with the modern lines (Eleanor Place 8 to 11 m off; the others 7 to 10 m) and were left out of the fit.
Berry Street is used as control; its modern line agrees to 1 to 5 m.
Woodbridge, Rahway Av to the Berry brickworks, 100 ft; Woodbridge Av, Moore, Berry. One part. Eleanor Place and the Wallace / Jean Court / Lillian Terrace block not used.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 shows the southern part of Woodbridge village between Amboy Avenue and the railroad at 100 feet to an inch. Amboy Avenue, lettered Amboy (Perth Amboy) Avenue, runs down the left side with Greenville (Grenville), Bergen, Sherry, Clinton and Bunns Lane crossing it at the left. The upper middle holds the quarter between 2nd Street, Coley, Spring and Albert, with Smith, Augustus and William running north to south: it is closely built with frame dwellings, Weiner and Company's bottling works, and the Hungarian Catholic Church. Caroline lies between Smith and Augustus, with the name Augusta printed in parentheses beside Augustus. Fulton runs down the right side beside the railroad, with Factory Lane (Berrys Lane) cutting across the upper right. The lower half is a laid-out subdivision of narrow unbuilt lots: Hampton Avenue, Milton Avenue, Earl, Russell, Strawberry Hill Avenue and Ruddy Place, with only a few dwellings along Milton Avenue and Fulton. A clay or terra cotta works stands at the lower right corner beside the railroad. A compass rose is at the upper right, the scale bar at the lower right, and a break line (A to B) runs near the bottom with sheet 22 beyond. Block numbers 434 to 456 and 642 to 644 are shown, with adjoining sheets 19, 20 and 22.
notes: Greenville (Grenville) is Grenville Street in OpenStreetMap; Smith is East Smith Street; Augusta is Augustus Street.
Hampton Avenue has no modern counterpart in the street data.

This sheet fits the modern streets poorly (RMSE about 4.8 m): the streets of the lower subdivision (Milton, Russell, Earl) and East Smith Street do not agree with the modern lines and Fulton Street was rebuilt with the railroad overpass, so the placement is low confidence.
Spring Street is marked not opened where it meets Augustus Street.

South Woodbridge, 100 ft; Albert, Caroline, Augustus, Milton, Amboy (Perth Amboy) Av. One part; weak fit (RMSE 4.8 m, every street subset and use_parcels false worse); seams with sheets 19, 20, 22 look continuous.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the outer part of Woodbridge south of the village, between Amboy Avenue and the railroad, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. It continues sheet 21 and begins at the break line A to B near the top. Most of the sheet is a laid-out subdivision of narrow lots, nearly all unbuilt, between Earl, Russell, Strawberry Hill Avenue and Fulton, which run north to south and are crossed by Benjamin near the top and by Cutters Dock Road (Cutters Lane) near the bottom. Amboy (Perth Amboy) Avenue runs down the left side, with Convery Boulevard branching south-west from it. Along the right side lie the main line of the railroad and heavy industry: M. D. Valentine and Bro. Co. makers of fire brick at the top, the Federal Seaboard Terra Cotta Company with its kilns and pressing shops in the middle, and the Bulls Ferry Chemical Company south of Cutters Dock Road. Below Cutters Dock Road are scattered buildings of the N. J. Wood Finishing Company varnish works and Castles Ice Cream Company on Amboy Avenue. A compass rose is at the right and the scale bar at the bottom right. The sheet carries the date February 1929 and the adjoining sheet number 21. Block numbers 455 to 468 are shown.
notes: Benjamin is Benjamin Street and Fulton is South Fulton Street in OpenStreetMap.
Only five control points were found, all in the middle of the sheet; the placement is medium confidence.
South Woodbridge, 100 ft; Benjamin, Strawberry Hill, Cutters Dock Rd, brick and terra cotta works. One part, 5 points.

sheet-23-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 23 shows the village of Sewaren, on the shore of Staten Island Sound at the east edge of Woodbridge Township, at 100 feet to an inch. It covers most of the sheet and is separated from a smaller part at the lower left by a heavy line. Woodbridge Avenue crosses the top; Sewaren Avenue, Robert, Charles, Arbor and George run in a block of narrow lots at the upper left, and West Avenue, lettered West (Sewaren) Avenue, runs south beside the railroad, which crosses the sheet diagonally from top to bottom as a group of parallel tracks. East of the tracks East Avenue runs south-west to north-east, with Broad, Holton, New and Ferry crossing the middle and lower right. Cliff Road runs down the right side along Smith's Creek and Staten Island Sound, past a row of shore lots. Almost all buildings are frame dwellings with a few boat houses on the shore; the sheet has no industry. The upper left is a laid-out subdivision with many unbuilt lots. A compass rose is at the right, a scale bar at the bottom right, and the title Sewaren is lettered at the top. Block numbers 469 to 483 and 801 are shown, with adjoining sheet 24.
notes: The railroad crossing the part gives a control point at Woodbridge Avenue (Garden State Secondary).
The junction of Arbor Street and West Avenue was rejected by the fit (9 m).
Sewaren, 100 ft. Part 1 main map. Part 2 lower left beyond the heavy line (Broad, Ferry, Cliff Road, Oakland Avenue, own north arrow): two-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-23-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 23 is the lower left corner of the sheet, cut off from the Sewaren map by a heavy line and drawn with its own north arrow, which points up and slightly to the right. It shows the western side of Sewaren at 100 feet to an inch. Ferry runs diagonally across the upper middle and Broad runs down the left edge. Cliff Road runs north to south at the centre beside Staten Island Sound, with a dock projecting into the water at its junction with Ferry. The lower left is a row of small frame dwellings on narrow lots along Oakland Avenue, with others on Broad. Block numbers 483 to 486 are shown, with the neighbouring blocks 477 and 484 above. The upper part is open land with a few buildings. The part has only two control points, both on Ferry, so its scale and rotation rest on them and agree with the other sheets only approximately.
notes: Placed from two junctions on Ferry Street (Broad Street and Cliff Road); the fit is a helmert and low confidence.
The scale of 4.05 px per foot and rotation of 13.9 degrees are close to those of the sheet's own north arrow.
Sewaren, 100 ft. Part 1 main map. Part 2 lower left beyond the heavy line (Broad, Ferry, Cliff Road, Oakland Avenue, own north arrow): two-point helmert, low confidence.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the village of Sewaren, in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned a few degrees from north. The sheet runs from Glencove Avenue and the open blocks at the top down to Woodbridge Avenue, which crosses the bottom, and from Grant Street and the block numbers on the west to Smith's Creek on the east. The streets are drawn as pairs of lines with long, narrow lots between them: Jersey Place, Pleasant Avenue, Calvin Avenue, Vernon, Robert and Summit Avenue run across the sheet, while Central Avenue, Sherman, Sewaren Avenue, Meade and a second street also lettered Sewaren Avenue run down it. Marsh, Brewster Place and Glencove Avenue lead east towards West Avenue. The western half is laid out in regular blocks, mostly vacant or lightly built with frame dwellings, and Public School No. 12 stands between Sherman and Sewaren Avenue. In the middle a Christian Science Society building is drawn on the long block between Marsh and Woodbridge Avenue. A trolley and public service right of way follows the street lettered Sewaren Avenue on the east side of the blocks. East of West Avenue the ground is open and carries the railroad, which runs diagonally from the upper right to Woodbridge Avenue, with a Sewaren depot and freight house beside it. Further east lie Cliff Road, East Avenue, a Motor Boat Club and St. John's Chapel on the shore of Smith's Creek, with the tidal marsh shown in blue. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches are marked on several streets. The sheet carries a compass rose, the Woodbridge Township cartouche dated February 1929 and a scale bar at the lower left; the area below Woodbridge Avenue is left blank for sheet 23.
notes: The street lettered Sewaren Avenue on the east side of the blocks (Sewaren Avenue near its upper end) is Old Road today; the street lettered Sewaren Avenue west of Meade is the modern Sewaren Avenue.

Pleasant Avenue is East Pleasant Avenue today, Calvin Avenue is Calvin Street, Robert is North Robert Street and South Robert Street, Summit Avenue is East Summit Avenue, and Sherman is Sherman Street.
Central Avenue's modern line lies several metres from the drawn one, so it was left out of the control points.
Sewaren, 100 ft; Sewaren Av, Pleasant, Calvin, Robert, Summit, Sherman, Grant, Meade, Marsh, West Av, Cliff Road. One part. Central Avenue left out (displaced).

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 shows the western part of Port Reading, in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north pointing to the upper left by about 25 to 30 degrees. The main street is Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road, which crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, and West Avenue, which runs down the right side past the Public School No. 9, an auditorium and gymnasium, and a fire company building. The northern part holds the closely built blocks of the village between Scott Place, Lee, Letitia Place and Division: rows of narrow lots with small frame dwellings, tile and brick works, a church and a number of dwellings along E Street, Irving (G St.), B Street and the streets lettered A, C and D that cross them. The Pennsylvania Railroad runs in a broad band across the top, beside the blocks bordering Randolph Place, Albert, Furman and John, which are mostly empty. To the southwest the sheet shows long, narrow lots laid out along A, B, C and D Streets and Vincent (Av.), most of them vacant, with a Home for the Aged and a block of dwellings on Blair Road (Boynton Av.). A Public Service trolley right of way, labelled as such, passes down the middle of the sheet. St. Anthony R.C. Church stands on Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road, and the small group of houses on Morris near the bottom edge sits among large vacant tracts. A large part of the lower area is vacant, and a stretch along the left edge is marked as exposed to the north. The sheet also carries a compass rose, the Woodbridge Township cartouche dated February 1929, the title Port Reading and a scale bar. The Sheet 26 key number appears in the upper margin and Old Road to Blazing Star at the lower right.

The street lettered Central Avenue west of Blair Road is probably Langford Avenue today (medium confidence).

A Street, B Street and E Street in the northern blocks are used as control under the same modern names; the C and D Street blocks and Vincent Avenue to the southwest lie where the New Jersey Turnpike runs today and have no modern equivalent.
Port Reading Avenue's modern line lies 4 to 5 m from the drawn road at Lee Street and E Street, so those junctions were left out of the control points.

sheet-26-1.description: Sheet 26 shows the central part of Port Reading, in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees from north (the compass rose at the upper left points to the upper left). The main feature is the planned grid of the village: parallel cross streets lettered 7th to 1st, from the top of the sheet down, are crossed by Carteret, Tappen and Turner running up and down the sheet. The blocks are cut into long, narrow lots numbered along their edges, and most of the northern blocks, between 7th Street and 4th Street, are empty paper with lot lines only. Houses, frame dwellings and a few stores are crowded on the blocks between 4th Street and 1st Street near Carteret and Tappen, with tile works and sheds shown in colour. Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right, with several railroad tracks and sidings beside it and a heavy black line that carries the main railroad across the sheet; a trestle is lettered beside it at the upper right. A building near the railroad at 1st Street is drawn in brown. A heavy line cuts off the lower right corner, which holds a separate part of the sheet (part 2). At the left, Turtle Brook Road, Berkeley, Cliff Avenue and Rahway Place bound large blocks cut into narrow lots, all vacant, and a bundle of railroad lines crosses the sheet near the lower edge. The Woodbridge Township cartouche dated February 1929 and the title Port Reading are at the top, and a scale bar is at the bottom. Sheet numbers 25 and 36 are written on blank areas where neighbouring sheets continue.
notes: Tappen is East Tappen Street today, Carteret is Carteret Street, and the numbered streets that survive are East 2nd, East 3rd, 4th, West 5th, East 5th and 7th Street; 1st Street keeps its name.
Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue today.
The blocks at the left (Turtle Brook Road, Berkeley, Rahway Place) are in the area of the New Jersey Turnpike and Renewal Way today and have no modern streets to control them.
East 5th Street / Turner Street is hand-picked (the detector did not find it); the same junction is drawn again on part 2.

Port Reading centre, 100 ft, north about 25 degrees left. Part 1 main grid (1st to 7th Streets, Carteret, Tappen, Turner). Part 2: lower right corner beyond the heavy line with its own north arrow (Turner to Vernon Way, 5th to 8th Streets, Holly, Larch), repeating ground at the right edge of part 1; split by the lead.

sheet-26-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 26 is the lower right corner of the sheet, cut off from the main Port Reading grid by a heavy line and given its own north arrow, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north about 25 degrees to the left like the main part. It continues the village east of Turner: 7th Street runs from the heavy line to Vernon Way, which crosses the corner diagonally, with Holly Street and Larch Street leading off it to the east toward sheet 36 and 8th Street at the top beside the railroad. Below 7th Street lie the long blocks 562 and 563, cut into narrow lots and almost empty, then 6th Street, 5th Street and Turner at the left, with a few frame dwellings and stores in blocks 564 and 565 near Turner. Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road with its water pipes crosses the bottom right corner diagonally. The corner repeats ground drawn at the right edge of part 1 (Turner between 5th and 7th Streets), shifted into the empty corner of the page; sheet 36 adjoins to the east. Most of the part is vacant lots; block 566 at the lower right is undivided.
notes: Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue; 5th Street at Turner is East 5th Street; 6th Street has no modern counterpart under that name.
Placed from four junctions (East 5th / Turner, 7th / Vernon Way, Larch / Vernon Way, Port Reading Avenue / Vernon Way); low to medium confidence.
Split from part 1 by the lead after the helper had configured the sheet as one part.

Port Reading centre, 100 ft, north about 25 degrees left. Part 1 main grid (1st to 7th Streets, Carteret, Tappen, Turner). Part 2: lower right corner beyond the heavy line with its own north arrow (Turner to Vernon Way, 5th to 8th Streets, Holly, Larch), repeating ground at the right edge of part 1; split by the lead.

sheet-27-1.description: Sheet 27 shows the eastern part of Port Reading at 100 feet to an inch. The upper part continues the grid of sheet 36: Holly and Larch run across between Henry and Grant, with frame dwellings in blocks 918 and 923 to 926, and the Borough Line, the boundary with Carteret, runs diagonally down to Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road, which crosses the sheet below them. South of the road, on the right, a small district of narrow lots lies between Edwin and the Carteret line along A Street (Essex), B Street (Union), C Street (Warren), D Street and Seymour, densely built with dwellings, a Hungarian Baptist Church, a coloured church and stores; a water tower with a standpipe stands on Edwin. The middle of the sheet is taken by the Port Reading railroad yard of the Philadelphia & Reading Railway, block 575, with many curving tracks and piles of railroad ties stacked 20 feet high. A heavy line boxes off the lower left of the sheet for an inset of the railway's creosoting plant (part 2), which is not part of this map. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 12 inches are marked along Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road and Edwin, and block numbers 573 to 581 and 918 to 926 appear with adjoining sheet 36.
notes: Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Grant is South East Grant Avenue.
A Street (Essex) is Essex Street, B Street (Union) Union Street, C Street (Warren) Warren Street; by their order along Edwin Street, D Street is today's Mercer Street and Seymour is Bergen Street.
The right edge is marked 'See Map of Carteret' and the Borough Line is drawn.

Port Reading east, 100 ft, rotation about +12. Part 1: Henry, Grant, Holly, Larch, Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road (Port Reading Avenue), Edwin with A (Essex), B (Union), C (Warren), D and Seymour Streets, the Port Reading yard. Part 2: boxed inset at lower left, Philadelphia & Reading Ry. creosoting plant, tracks only.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the middle of Fords, in Woodbridge Township, from Pitman Avenue at the top to King George's Post Road, Clum Avenue and Joyce Place at the lower right, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. The sheet is turned so that north lies up and to the left, and a compass rose stands at the left edge. The upper half is thinly built: very large blocks cut into narrow lots along Pitman, Dunbar, Summit and Woodland Avenues, with only scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings, between Mary Avenue on the west and Poplar and Liberty on the east. Beech and Poplar run north-northwest to south-southeast across these blocks. The lower half is a close grid of small lots on Mary Avenue, Bensonhurst Avenue, Izola Avenue, Hanson Avenue, Walnut, Beech, Elm, Pine, Oak and Ivy, with rows of small frame and a few brick dwellings and a few stores near Hanson Avenue. King George's Post Road crosses the lower right diagonally, with Hoy Avenue and Livingston Avenue joining it at the bottom. Woodbridge Public School No. 1, a large brick building, stands on the block between King George's Post Road, Hoy Avenue and Clum Avenue. Clum Avenue, Crows Mill Road and Joyce Place bound a set of narrow lots at the lower right, where the Princeton Map Division stamp covers part of the sheet. Six-inch water pipes are marked in many of the streets. Block numbers 582 to 609 and 700 to 705 appear, with adjoining sheets 37, 29 and 30.
notes: King George's Post Road is King Georges Road today.

In OpenStreetMap Elm and Pine are South Elm Street and South Pine Street, Livingston Avenue is South Livingston Avenue, Linden Avenue is Linden Street and Beech, Poplar, Walnut, Ivy, Grover and Liberty are Streets.
Woodbridge Public School No. 1 is on this sheet.

The first bootstrap points read off the overview put the fit on the wrong junctions (RMSE 7 m, 4.25 px/ft); with the fit anchored at Beech / Dunbar, Beech / Pitman and Clum Avenue / Joyce Place it is 1.4 m at 3.97 px/ft.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the south-western part of Fords, from Evergreen Avenue and Linden Avenue at the top to Saffron Avenue at the bottom, between Jefferson Avenue on the west and the streets east of King George's Post Road. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the lower part from edge to edge; King George's Post Road comes in from the upper right and joins it at a fork near the bottom right. A dash-dot township line crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the fork. The upper left is thinly built, with frame dwellings, some with poultry houses, on large lots along Evergreen Avenue, Wildwood Avenue and 5th Street. The right-hand half is a dense grid of small frame dwellings on 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th Streets, Grant Avenue and Hall Street. A Greek Catholic church and a bank stand near the Post Road, and the Church and School of Our Lady of Peace stands at Maple Avenue. Stores and shops line New Brunswick Avenue near the fork, with an auto repair shop, a meter house and a truck garage on the block to the south. South of New Brunswick Avenue the blocks are large and mostly empty, and Delta and Eaton are lettered Arbitrary. Block numbers 709 to 734 appear, with adjoining sheets 28, 30 and 37.
notes: Saffron Avenue is Safran Avenue today, and New Brunswick Avenue west of the fork is Amboy Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
King George's Post Road is King Georges Road today.
The north end of Jefferson Avenue is lettered Av. (Delhi).
Amboy Avenue junctions with Jefferson, Bloomfield, Franklin and Maple were 8 to 13 m from the fit and were left out by the detector: the modern line of Amboy Avenue may differ from the drawn street.
Church and School of Our Lady of Peace R.C. and a Greek Catholic church are on this sheet.
Fords SW, 100 ft; Amboy / New Brunswick Av and King George's Post Rd fork; township line. One part. Amboy Avenue junctions west of the fork rejected (8-13 m); South Ridgedale Place left out.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the central-south part of Fords, from King George's Post Road and Livingstone Avenue at the top to the Lehigh Valley Railroad at the bottom, between Corrielle Street on the west and Hornsby Street and Crows Mill Road on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left. King George's Post Road runs diagonally across the upper left, with a fan of narrow-lot streets (Fairfield Avenue, Mary Avenue, Woodland Avenue, Oakland Avenue) to its north-west. East of Hoy Avenue and Egan, regular blocks run between Livingstone Avenue, Fairfield Avenue, Maxwell Avenue and Hamilton Avenue, mostly with small frame dwellings on 25 foot lots. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the sheet below the middle with stores, a motion picture house and shops along its north side near Corrielle Street. South of it, small dwellings fill the blocks on Ling, Paul, Ryan and William Streets down to the Lehigh Valley Railroad, drawn as a bundle of tracks along the bottom edge. Churches and institutions include the Slovak Presbyterian Church, St. John's Mission Episcopal, and Grace Evangelical Lutheran Parish Hall. Smith and Ostergaard Builders have a lumber yard near Hamilton Avenue. Block numbers 598 to 749 appear, with adjoining sheets 28, 29 and 31.
notes: King George's Post Road is King Georges Road today; Livingstone Avenue is South Livingston Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad along the bottom is lettered L.V.R.R.
Slovak Presbyterian Church, St. John's Mission Episcopal and Grace Evangelical Lutheran Parish Hall are on this sheet.
Fords centre-south to the L.V.R.R., 100 ft. One part.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 covers the eastern part of Fords, from Johnson Street and Livingston Avenue at the top to the Lehigh Valley Railroad at the bottom, between Hornsby Street on the west and a large cemetery on the east. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the sheet in the lower half. Above it, Crow's Mill Road and Liberty run north-northwest across a set of narrow-lot blocks on Johnson, Lawrence, Corey, Olive, Beaver, Parker and Adams, mostly open with scattered frame dwellings. The block north-east of Liberty has a long run of lots, and the east side of the sheet is taken up by the cemetery with Oregon Avenue along its edge. A cigar factory stands on Crow's Mill Road at New Brunswick Avenue. Below New Brunswick Avenue, the blocks between Hornsby, Lillian, Louis, Grace, Voorhees, Fraser and Grant carry small frame dwellings with a few shops, a club house and an electric substation on William Street, and a coal yard on the south side of William. The railroad is drawn as a band of tracks, crossed by the road that runs south to a bridge. Block numbers 22 to 32 and 750 to 767 appear, with adjoining sheets 30 and 32.
notes: Louis, Voorhees, Fraser and Grant are lettered with a second name in parentheses (Celina, Cleves, Liberty, Branch).
Crow's Mill Road is Crows Mill Road today, and Fraser, Louis, Voorhees and Grant are Fraser Street, South Louis Street, Voorhees Street and South Grant Street in OpenStreetMap.
Crows Mill Road / Maxwell Avenue was 9 m from the fit and was left out.
Fords east, New Brunswick Av to the L.V.R.R., cemetery at right, 100 ft. One part.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the western part of Hopelawn, in Woodbridge Township, from School Street at the top to William Street at the bottom, between the cemetery and Oregon Avenue on the left and Weidner Avenue and Geraldine on the right. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left, with a compass rose at the left. The upper two thirds is a subdivision of very long narrow lots numbered in the 15 to 60 range, with streets running north-northwest (Pennsylvania Avenue, John) crossed by Clyde Avenue, Howard, James, Worden Avenue, Lee, Luther Avenue, Loretta and Juliette Street. Only a few frame dwellings stand on it, mostly on the lower and eastern blocks. New Brunswick Avenue crosses the sheet below, lined with small frame dwellings and a few shops between Columbus Avenue, Jersey, Commercial, Erin Avenue and Emmet Avenue, with a feed mill and a mill building at Erin Avenue. The Handkerchief Manufacturing Company's plant stands at the right on New Brunswick Avenue. Douglass and William run along the lower left, and Pennsylvania Avenue and Weidner Avenue continue south of New Brunswick Avenue through large undivided blocks. Block numbers 762 to 787 appear, with adjoining sheets 31, 33 and 34.
notes: Jersey is lettered Jersey (New Jersey) Avenue, and Commercial is lettered Commercial (Av.).

Columbus Avenue, Jersey, Erin Avenue, Emmet Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue are South Columbus Avenue, Jersey Avenue, Erin Avenue, Emmett Avenue and Pennsylvania Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Weidner Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Handkerchief Manufacturing Company is on this sheet.
Hopelawn west, New Brunswick Av and long-lot subdivision, 100 ft. One part.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the eastern part of Hopelawn, from Worden Avenue at the top left to New Brunswick Avenue, with a large unbuilt tract below, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left. The right edge follows Florida Grove Road along the boundary with the City of Perth Amboy, with a note to see the map of Perth Amboy. The built area is a grid of long narrow lots, 25 feet wide, in blocks between John, Herbert, Ellen (Street) Avenue and Charles on Worden Avenue, Lee, Luther Avenue, Loretta, Juliette and May Streets. The dwellings are mostly small frame houses, with a poultry house and a few outbuildings in the upper left. Near the boundary at the right edge are a stone yard, a slaughter house and a hall. New Brunswick Avenue runs along the bottom of the built area. Below it, one block number, 787, covers a very large unsubdivided tract with Weidner Avenue along its left edge, down to the Lehigh Valley Railroad (Pa. Branch) with a yard full of tracks at the bottom. Block numbers 781 to 801 appear, with adjoining sheets 32 and 34.
notes: The street lettered Ellen (St.) Av. is Ellen Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Charles is South Charles Street.
The boundary is lettered City of Perth Amboy, and the right margin reads See Map of Perth Amboy.
The railroad at the bottom is lettered L.V.R.R. (Pa. Branch), yard full of tracks.
Hopelawn east to the Perth Amboy boundary, 100 ft; large unbuilt block below New Brunswick Av. One part.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the north-eastern corner of Hopelawn, between Florida Grove Road and the City of Perth Amboy boundary on the right and the cemetery and large unsubdivided blocks to the west, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north lies up and to the left. The top third is mostly empty: the Old Road to New Brunswick crosses it with a few scattered frame buildings and farm outbuildings, and the blocks 802 and 803 and a cemetery fill the rest. In the middle, Public School No. 10, a large brick building, stands on the north side of Clyde Avenue (Street). South of Clyde Avenue the sheet is a dense grid of narrow lots between John and Charles, on Howard, James and Worden Avenue, with rows of small frame dwellings and a few outbuildings; Herbert is lettered not open north of Clyde. Louis, Spa (Ada) and Alton are marked not open along the left side. A church or hall in blue stands near Charles at the right edge. Florida Grove Road bends at the top right and continues down the right edge, lettered Perth Amboy Road where it turns south-east. Block numbers 802 to 814 appear, with adjoining sheets 32 and 33.
notes: Spa is lettered Spa (Ada); Louis, Spa and Alton are marked not open.
Clyde Avenue (Street) is Clyde Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Florida Grove is Florida Grove Road.
The boundary is lettered City of Perth Amboy, and the right margin reads See Map of Perth Amboy.
Public School No. 10 is on this sheet.
Hopelawn NE, 100 ft; school No. 10; top third mostly empty (cemetery, Old Road to New Brunswick). One part. Louis Street left out.

sheet-36-1.description: The upper part of sheet 36 shows the northern blocks of Port Reading, in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and almost square to north. It lies above a heavy dividing line that separates it from the Iselin part below. A regular grid of long blocks, numbered 901 to 921, is laid out between Vernon Way on the left edge and Henry on the right. Birch, Spruce, Holly and Larch cross the sheet from side to side, with Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road running slightly slanted along the bottom of the part. The blocks are cut into narrow lots, numbered along the edges, and most of the grid is vacant. Houses cluster between Hagaman, Daniel and Marion on the blocks around Spruce and Holly, and a small dwelling marked tile stands on the Birch block near the top. A temporary school with a class room building is drawn on block 911. At the upper right the grid ends where Division and Henry run off at an angle, and the blocks there (908, 913, 917, 920) are cut diagonally; a dash-dot line crossing the corner is lettered as the boundary of the Borough of Carteret. The Woodbridge Township cartouche dated February 1929 and the title Port Reading are in the top margin, a north arrow is at the right, and the key numbers 26 and 27 stand on the neighbouring sheets' edges. Sheet 26 continues to the left and below on the Port Reading grid.
notes: Woodbridge & Roosevelt Road is Port Reading Avenue today; Hagaman, Daniel, Marion and Henry are Hagaman Street, Daniel Street, Marion Street and Henry Street; Birch, Spruce, Holly and Larch are Birch Street, Spruce Street, Holly Street and Larch Street.
The sheet carries a printed north arrow; the fitted rotation is about 1 degree counter-clockwise from the page's vertical.

100 ft, two parts far apart on the ground divided by a heavy line: part 1 Port Reading (Vernon Way to Henry, Birch to Larch); part 2 Iselin (Green / Oak Tree Rd, Berkeley Blvd, Cooper to Benjamin, Worth, Indiana), anchored on Benjamin / Green, low confidence.

sheet-36-2.description: The lower part of sheet 36 shows the village of Iselin, in Woodbridge Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 12 degrees from north. It lies below a heavy dividing line that separates it from the Port Reading part above, and Green (Oak Tree Rd.) forms the top edge. Cooper Av., Ridgley Av., Elmhurst Av. and Benjamin Av. run down the sheet across the numbered blocks 214, 215, 216 and 221 to 223, and Berkeley Blvd. crosses them near the bottom; Middlesex & Essex Turnpike runs diagonally along the upper left, and Worth, Indiana Av. and Berkeley Av. are on the right. The lots are narrow and numbered; the built-up frontage is along Cooper Av., Ridgley Av. and the top of the blocks below Green, with small frame dwellings and a few buildings drawn in colour. The lower blocks and the diagonal blocks at the left and right are vacant lots only. The word Iselin is lettered across a block on the right. A 6 inch water pipe is drawn along several of the avenues. The sheet carries a compass rose at the left, a scale bar at the bottom and the key number 3 beside Green. The place is far to the west of the Port Reading part above, and the two are not connected on the ground.
notes: Green (Oak Tree Rd.) is Green Street and Oak Tree Road today; Middlesex & Essex Turnpike is Middlesex-Essex Turnpike; Indiana Av. is Indiana Avenue and West Indiana Avenue; Ridgley Av., Berkeley Blvd. and Berkeley Av. are not in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Placed from a single measured junction (Benjamin Avenue and Green Street) with the atlas scale; low confidence, since all the usable junctions lie along Green.

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 covers the north-western part of Fords, from Murdock Avenue and Evergreen Avenue to Pitman Avenue and Linden Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch on a yellowed scan. It is turned slightly so that north lies up and a little to the left. Ford Avenue runs from top to bottom on the left with Drummond Avenue and Cutter Avenue beside it, and Main Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. The streets in the right half (Summit Avenue, Dunbar Avenue, Woodland Avenue, Linden Avenue, Grant Avenue and Mary Avenue) enclose large blocks with only a few frame dwellings, while the blocks along Ford Avenue, Drummond Avenue and Cutter Avenue have scattered frame dwellings and outbuildings on long lots. Public School No. 14, a brick building, stands at Main Street and Ford Avenue. The Trenton-Fords Art Stone Company, manufacturers of cast stone, stands between Vine and Grant Avenue; its watchman has no clock and heat, steam, lights and power are electric. The closed plant of the Pacer Aircraft Corporation stands on Grant Avenue north of Summit Avenue. Rows of dwellings line Hollister Place and Evergreen Avenue at the lower left. Six-inch and twelve-inch water pipes are marked. Block numbers 51 to 63, 582, 590, 707 and 710 appear, with adjoining sheets 28 and 29.
notes: Murdock Avenue is Murdock Street in OpenStreetMap; Main, Vine and Linden Avenue are Main Street, Vine Street and Linden Street.
Public School No. 14 and the Trenton-Fords Art Stone Company are on this sheet.
